get.summary: The signed-in buyer's company, role and account
get.description:
The company the account buys for, its role there, and where the company's account stands. A 403 means the account buys for no company — the storefront's cue to treat the shopper as a retail one. `credit.limit` and `credit.available` are null when the company has no account and pays up front.

Like every route here that needs a buyer, it first compares the account's address with the one it joined under: a changed address leaves the company's customer group, and the new one joins once identity has confirmed it.
Every buyer of the caller's company with their role, oldest first, names read from their accounts. Any buyer may read it. Not paginated.

patch.description: Company admins only. The last admin cannot be demoted: a company nobody can administer is one only the store can rescue.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is not its admin (`forbidden`).

404.description: That account is not a buyer for this company.

409.description: It is the company's last admin.

delete.summary: Remove a buyer, or leave the company
delete.description: An admin may remove anybody, and any buyer may remove themselves: somebody who has left the company should not need an admin to stop buying for it. The account's address leaves the company's customer group, so its next cart is priced as anybody's. The last admin can neither leave nor be removed here; the store can, through `DELETE /api/admin/x/b2b/companies/{id}/members/{customer_id}`.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is removing somebody else without being an admin (`forbidden`).

404.description: That account is not a buyer for this company.

409.description: It is the company's last admin.

get.description: Company admins only. Invitations not yet accepted and not expired, newest first. Not paginated. The token is never returned.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is not its admin (`forbidden`).

post.summary: Invite somebody to buy for the company
post.description:
Company admins only. Emails the address: the notification event `b2b.invitation` carries `invite_token` and, when the store configured an invitation page, `invite_url`. The token is never in the response — it went to the mailbox, and only the mailbox should have it. An invitation stays open for a week unless the store configured otherwise. A second invitation to the same address replaces the first, so only the newest link works.

The invitation is sent even when the address already belongs to a confirmed account: joining is accepting it, with `POST /x/b2b/invitations/accept`.

400.description: `role` is not admin, approver or buyer, or `email` is not an address.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is not its admin (`forbidden`).

delete.description: Company admins only. The emailed link stops working.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is not its admin (`forbidden`).

404.description: No open invitation with that id for this company.

post.summary: Accept an invitation and join the company
post.description: The one route here the caller need not already be a buyer for: it is how they become one. The signed-in account's address must be the one the invitation was mailed to — a forwarded link is refused. The token reached that mailbox, so accepting it proves the account reads it: identity marks the address confirmed (`email_verified: true`), the account joins with the invitation's role, and its address joins the company's customer group, so its carts are priced on the company's terms from then on. An account buys for one company at a time.

token.description: The token from the invitation email, or from the link it carried.

400.description: The token is unknown, already used or expired (`invalid_token`).

403.description: The invitation was mailed to another address; sign in as that address to accept it (`forbidden`).

409.description: The account already buys for another company.

post.summary: Place the buyer's cart for their company
post.description:
The cart is first priced as the buyer — their company's customer-group prices, through the address identity has confirmed — and then placed with the company's rules applied to the final total, inside the checkout's own transaction: a refusal means no order exists, not one cancelled afterwards.

`payment_method` defaults to `on_account` when the company has an account (a credit limit), and must be given when it has none. On account nothing is charged: `payment.kind` is `none`, the payment stays pending until the store marks the order paid, and the order falls due `net_days` after it was placed. `on_account` exists only on this module's routes: `GET /api/checkout` does not list it, and the public checkout refuses it.

An order over the company's approval threshold, placed by somebody whose role is `buyer`, is not placed. It is filed as a request for approval holding the basket at its prices, the company's approvers and admins are emailed (`b2b.approval_requested`), and the answer is 202 with `approval`. Admins and approvers never wait. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key replays the order, or answers with the request already filed.

A basket priced as a company's buyer cannot be placed around this route: `POST /api/checkout/{code}` refuses it with 403 `company_checkout_required`.

`line_ids` checks out only those lines of the cart. They are copied into a basket of their own — on the same storefront, priced as the buyer, with the cart's discount code — and that basket is checked out exactly as above, limits and approvals included. The lines leave the cart only once they are an order; a request for approval filed instead leaves the cart as it was. A retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` replays the order or the request.

400.description: `cart_id` is missing; the company has no account and no `payment_method` was given; the company requires a purchase-order number and `po_number` is empty; or the address is incomplete; or a `line_ids` entry is not a line of this cart, is listed twice, or is not a positive integer.

403.description: The account buys for no company; the company is closed; a line is outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`, with each such line in `details` as `{variant_id, sku, reason}`); `on_account` was chosen and the company is on hold or has no account; the order would take the company past its credit limit (`credit_limit_exceeded`, the message saying how much is available, in minor units); or the buyer's address is not confirmed (`email_unverified`). A catalogue is checked before the approval threshold, so a basket holding a line outside it is refused rather than filed for an approver.

404.description: No such cart, or no such payment method.

409.description: The cart is no longer valid at these prices, with per-line detail as `POST /api/checkout/{code}` gives it — a partial checkout reports a line that would not go into its basket the same way — or it has already been checked out; or part of this cart is already being checked out.

get.description:
The caller's company's account over a period, for its admins and approvers; a plain buyer is refused. Every order placed on account is a debit on the day it was placed; a payment is a credit on the day the store recorded it; a payment taken back as recorded in error (`payment_reversed`) is a debit again; and an order cancelled while still owed is a credit. A payment is dated from core's own record of it — the event written in the transaction that marked the order paid, delivered to the module or read back from the order's history — and `date_source` is `recorded`. A payment with no record left (an order imported already paid, an event deleted) is dated the moment the module first saw it and marked `noticed`: it was paid at or before then. What is owed is worked out as the credit check works it out — on account, neither paid nor cancelled — so a statement ending today closes on the outstanding figure.

`from` is the first day and `to` the day after the last, as every date range in the engine is, both civil dates in the store's time zone (its profile's, UTC when it has none). Leaving both out is the month to date. `aging` is what is owed at the end, by whole days past due in the store's calendar: due on the 30th is current on the 30th.

200.description: The statement. With `format=csv`, the same as a file: one table, the opening balance its first row and the closing balance and aging buckets its last, each named in `kind` with the amount in `balance_minor`.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is a plain buyer: a statement is for whoever runs the account.

get.summary: What the company may buy, at the buyer's prices
get.description: The products on sale that the caller's company may buy — its catalogue's, or every one when it has none — by title, each with its active variants and what one costs in a basket priced as this buyer: core's own price resolution (`Pricing.PriceInChannel`) for the address the company's group holds for them, on the default storefront a quick order opens its basket on. A quantity break lowers it in the basket. A product on sale whose every variant is switched off has nothing to buy and is left out, from the page and from the total. Any buyer of the company may read it. A catalogue is what a company held to it may buy: every product filed under one of its categories or anything beneath them — read from core's category tree as it stands at the moment of the check — and its products one by one. A company with no catalogue buys everything. The checkout guard, quick order, a file, a repeat order and a quote all hold to it; the public storefront still lists every product to a signed-in company buyer, and the guard is what holds the line.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the title or of a variant's SKU, in any case.

parameters.name: category_id
parameters.description: Only this category and everything under it. Anything but a positive integer is a 400.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The same as `limit`, which wins when both are sent.

200.description: A page of products the company may buy.

get.summary: The categories the company's catalogue can be browsed by
get.description: Every category holding at least one product the caller's company may buy — the products `GET /x/b2b/catalogue` lists — and the categories above them, ordered by full name. `product_count` counts what is filed under a category at any depth, which is what `category_id` on the catalogue returns. A company held to a catalogue sees only the branches it may buy from; one with none sees every category that holds a product on sale. Any buyer of the company may read it.

Orders placed for the company, newest first. An admin or approver sees every buyer's; a buyer sees their own. Each row says whether it was placed on account, when it falls due, and whether it is overdue.

get.summary: One of the company's orders, with what was in it
get.description: An order from the company's list, by the rule the list applies — their own to a buyer, any of the company's to an admin or approver — with the order itself as its shopper is shown it: lines, address, figures and shipments, without the store's note to itself or its record of returns. This is what a buyer reads before repeating an order.

404.description: No such order in the company's list, or one placed by a colleague of a buyer, who sees only their own.

get.description: Newest first. An admin or approver sees the company's; a buyer sees their own.
A buyer may read only the requests they filed; anybody else's is a 404, as another company's is.

post.summary: Approve a request and place its order
post.description:
Approvers and admins only. Places the order on the requester's behalf from the request's snapshot: its lines at the prices the approver was shown, with the payment method, PO number and address the buyer gave; delivery and tax are worked out again as of now. The approval threshold no longer applies; the credit limit and the company's status still do.

The request is claimed before anything is placed, so two approvers approving at once place it once and the second gets 409. If the order cannot be placed — stock gone, the credit limit used up since, the requester no longer a buyer for the company, the quote it came from no longer on offer — the request goes back to `pending` with the reason in `last_error`, and that refusal is the answer. On success the requester is emailed (`b2b.approval_decided`).

The order is under `order.order`: `order` is the same `{order, payment}` pair a checkout answers with.

201.description: Approved, and the order placed: the same order and payment a checkout answers with, and the approval that placed it.

403.description: The account buys for no company or its role is `buyer` (`forbidden`); or placing the order was refused — the company is closed; a line is outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`, with each such line in `details` as `{variant_id, sku, reason}`), the catalogue having narrowed since the request was made; it is on hold with `on_account` chosen; or the order is over its credit limit (`credit_limit_exceeded`).

404.description: No such request for this company.

409.description: The request is no longer pending; the requester no longer buys for the company; the quote it came from expired (`quote_expired`) or is otherwise not on offer; or a line can no longer be sold.

post.description: Approvers and admins only. The `reason`, if one is given, is kept on the request and emailed to the requester (`b2b.approval_decided`). The body may be left out altogether.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or its role is `buyer` (`forbidden`).

404.description: No such request for this company.

409.description: The request is no longer pending.

post.description: Only the buyer who filed it may: an approver who does not want it rejects it, and says why. Nobody is emailed.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or did not file this request (`forbidden`).

404.description: No such request for this company.

409.description: The request is no longer pending.

get.description: Newest first. An admin or approver sees the company's; a buyer sees the ones they asked for.

post.description: Any buyer of the company may ask, whatever their role. A request carries variants and quantities, never prices: a `unit_price_minor` on a line is accepted and thrown away, because what a buyer would like to pay is not what the store offers. The quote starts `requested`; the store prices it and sends it, and the buyer is emailed when it is ready (`b2b.quote_ready`).

400.description: No lines, a line without a positive quantity, a variant listed twice, or a variant that does not exist.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or the company is closed (`forbidden`); or a line is outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`, with each such line in `details` as `{variant_id, sku, reason}`).

get.description: A buyer may read only the quotes they asked for; anybody else's is a 404, as another company's is.

post.summary: Accept a quote and place its order
post.description:
Places the order at the quoted prices, under the rules a checkout meets: the company's status, its credit limit, a required PO number. `payment_method` defaults to `on_account` when the company has an account. The quote is claimed first, so two accepts at once place one order; it becomes `accepted`, with the order's id and number on it.

A quote over the company's approval threshold, accepted by somebody whose role is `buyer`, is filed for approval instead — 202 with `approval`, of kind `quote` — and the quote waits as `awaiting_approval` until an approver places it, or goes back to `quoted` if the approval is rejected or withdrawn.

The buyer who asked may accept it, and so may an admin or approver; to anybody else it is a 404.

400.description: The company has no account and no `payment_method` was given; a PO number is required and `po_number` is empty; or the address is incomplete.

403.description: The account buys for no company; or placing the order was refused — the company is closed; a line is outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`, with each such line in `details` as `{variant_id, sku, reason}`); `on_account` was chosen and the company is on hold or has no account; or the order is over its credit limit (`credit_limit_exceeded`).

404.description: No such quote for this company, or no such payment method.

409.description: The quote expired (`quote_expired`) — ask for it to be quoted again — or is not on offer: not sent yet, already accepted, or declined.

post.description: Closes the quote without an order, whether it was still waiting for a price or already sent. `declined_by` records the buyer's address. The buyer who asked may decline it, and so may an admin or approver; to anybody else it is a 404. Nobody is emailed.

404.description: No such quote for this company.

409.description: The quote is already accepted, declined or cancelled.

post.summary: Put a pasted order, or a spreadsheet, into the basket
post.description:
Quick order: up to 500 lines by SKU or variant id, added one by one through the same rules as the public cart routes, into the basket named by `cart_id` or a new one. The basket is priced as the buyer first, so every line goes in at their company's price.

The body is JSON, or a spreadsheet sent as `text/csv` with the basket named in the `cart_id` query parameter. A file's first row names its columns — `sku` or `variant_id`, and `quantity` — in any case and any order, with any byte-order mark ignored; other columns are ignored too, so an export with titles and prices beside the SKUs still reads. Empty rows are skipped. It is read by core's CSV reader, which takes off the apostrophe an export put before a cell beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. A file with no such header, or that cannot be parsed, is a 400 naming the problem.

A line that cannot go in — a SKU nobody sells, something not for sale, more than is in stock, a quantity under 1 or not a number, a product outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`) — is listed in `rejected` with its reason, and from a file with its `row`; the rest still go in, and the answer is 200 whatever was rejected. Adding a SKU already in the basket adds to its quantity.

Nothing is placed; check the basket out with `POST /x/b2b/checkout`.

400.description: `lines` is empty or longer than 500, or the body is malformed; or a file has no header naming `quantity` and `sku` or `variant_id`, no lines under it, more than 500, or a row the CSV parser cannot read.

403.description: The account buys for no company; the company is closed; or the buyer's address is not confirmed (`email_unverified`), so the basket cannot be priced as them.

409.description: The basket has already been checked out.

parameters.name: cart_id
parameters.description: With a `text/csv` body, the basket to fill; absent opens a new one. A JSON body names it in its own `cart_id`.

post.summary: Repeat an order, at today's prices
post.description:
Puts a past order's lines into a basket — the one `cart_id` names, or a new one — priced as the buyer today — never at the order's own prices, which may have been a quote's or a list since changed. A line that can no longer be bought is listed in `rejected`, as a pasted order's is. Nothing is placed: the basket is checked out like any other, through the same limits and approvals.

The order must be in the company's order list and the caller's to see there: their own to a buyer, any to an admin or approver.

cart_id.description: The basket to add the order's lines to, by its token, beside what it already holds. Absent opens a new one.

403.description: The account buys for no company; the company is closed; or the buyer's address is not confirmed (`email_unverified`).

404.description: No such order in the company's list, or one placed by a colleague of a buyer, who sees only their own.

get.description: Enquiries routed to the caller's company, newest first, with the customer's details unmasked: they are the dealer's to answer. An admin or approver only — a buyer orders for the company and does not see its leads.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is a buyer rather than an admin or approver.

post.summary: Send an enquiry to the dealer who covers an address
post.description:
The storefront's "find a dealer" form, and the one route here that needs no session. The enquiry goes to the dealer whose territory covers the address — the most specific match: a territory naming a state outranks one that does not, and within that the longest postcode prefix wins — among dealers that are not closed. An on-hold dealer still sells, so it still receives. When nobody covers the address the store keeps it. The dealer's admins and approvers are emailed (`b2b.lead_routed`).

The answer is the same 202 whoever the enquiry went to, and whether it went to anybody: naming the dealer would let anyone map the dealer network a postcode at a time.

Limited per peer address — ten a minute unless the store configured otherwise — counting every attempt, valid or not. The address is the connection's, never `X-Forwarded-For`.

400.description: A field is too long or has control characters in it; neither `email` nor `phone` was given; one is malformed; `country` is not a two-letter code; the variant or product does not exist; or the body has a field the form does not.

429.description: Too many enquiries from this address (`too_many_attempts`). `Retry-After` says how many seconds until the next is accepted.

patch.description: A dealer's admin or approver reporting back on one of its leads. Another dealer's lead is a 404: dealers do not learn about each other's customers.

400.description: `status` is not new, contacted, won or lost.

403.description: The account buys for no company, or is a buyer rather than an admin or approver.

404.description: No such lead among the company's.

get.description: Requires companies.read. Newest first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches part of the name, in any case, or part of the code.

parameters.name: dealers
parameters.description: `true` keeps only the companies with at least one territory: the dealers.

post.description: Requires companies.write, which by default only a manager holds: setting a credit limit is lending the store's money. Only `name` is required; `code` is made from the name when left out. A company without `credit_limit_minor` has no account and pays up front; without `approval_threshold_minor` its buyers never wait for approval. `group_id` names the customer group whose prices the company's buyers get (`/api/admin/customer-groups`); the module adds and removes buyers' addresses there itself.

400.description: `name` is missing; `code` is not lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens; `status` or `net_days` is out of range; an amount is negative; or the customer group does not exist.

409.description: A company with that code already exists.

get.description: Requires companies.read.

patch.description: Requires companies.write. Every field is optional and an omitted one is left alone; `null` on `group_id`, `credit_limit_minor` or `approval_threshold_minor` clears it — no customer group, no account, no approval rule. `metadata`, when given, replaces the whole object. Moving the company to another customer group moves every buyer's address with it, so their carts are priced on the new terms from their next checkout.

400.description: `name` is empty; `code` is not lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens; `status` or `net_days` is out of range; an amount is negative; or the customer group does not exist.

409.description: Another company already has that code.

delete.description: Requires companies.write. Its buyers' addresses leave its customer group, and its buyers, invitations, requests for approval and quotes go with it. A company with orders on its books is refused: the ledger would lose whose orders they were. Close it instead, with `status: closed`.

409.description: The company has orders on its books.

get.description: Requires companies.read. What is outstanding is read from the orders themselves: placed on account, neither paid nor cancelled. `limit` and `available` are null when the company has no account.

Requires companies.read. Every change to a company's terms — status, credit limit, net days, approval threshold, whether a PO is required, customer group and catalogue — newest first, written in the same transaction as the change: the field, its old and new value as the API takes them (`null` is none), who made it and when. A company's first terms are recorded as `action: created` with no old value. Money fields carry `currency`. `actor_kind` is `operator` (somebody signed in, or an API key, with their address), `token` (a static admin token), `buyer` (one of the company's own admins) or `system`.

Requires companies.read. Every order placed on account is a debit on the day it was placed; a payment is a credit on the day the store recorded it; a payment taken back as recorded in error (`payment_reversed`) is a debit again; and an order cancelled while still owed is a credit. A payment is dated from core's own record of it — the event written in the transaction that marked the order paid, delivered to the module or read back from the order's history — and `date_source` is `recorded`. A payment with no record left (an order imported already paid, an event deleted) is dated the moment the module first saw it and marked `noticed`: it was paid at or before then. What is owed is worked out as the credit check works it out — on account, neither paid nor cancelled — so a statement ending today closes on the outstanding figure.

`from` is the first day and `to` the day after the last, as every date range in the engine is, both civil dates in the store's time zone (its profile's, UTC when it has none). Leaving both out is the month to date. `aging` is what is owed at the end, by whole days past due in the store's calendar: due on the 30th is current on the 30th.

200.description: The statement. With `format=csv`, the same as a file: one table, the opening balance its first row and the closing balance and aging buckets its last, each named in `kind` with the amount in `balance_minor`.

get.description: Requires companies.read. Oldest first, not paginated. Addresses are masked on a demo store, as on every admin route.

post.summary: Add a buyer, or invite one
post.description: Requires companies.write. An account whose address identity has already confirmed joins at once: 201 with `member`. Anybody else — no account yet, or an address not confirmed — is invited instead, because the address is about to be given the company's prices and nothing has proved it: 202 with `invitation`, and an email goes to the address (`b2b.invitation`) carrying a link or a token the API never returns. The invitation names the signed-in operator as who sent it, or `the store` for a static token.

201.description: Added. `member` is set and `invitation` is absent.

202.description: Invited. `invitation` is set and `member` is absent.

400.description: `role` is not admin, approver or buyer, or `email` is not an address.

409.description: The account already buys for another company.

patch.description: Requires companies.write. The last admin cannot be demoted. The address in the answer is masked on a demo store.

404.description: The account is not a buyer for this company.

409.description: It is the company's last admin.

delete.description: Requires companies.write. Their address leaves the company's customer group. Unlike the buyers' own route this removes the last admin too: the store is who rescues a company nobody can administer.

404.description: The account is not a buyer for this company.

get.description: Requires companies.read. Not accepted and not expired, newest first; not paginated. The token is never returned, and addresses are masked on a demo store. A company that does not exist has no invitations: the answer is an empty list, not a 404.

delete.description: Requires companies.write. The emailed link stops working.

404.description: No open invitation with that id for this company.

get.description: Requires companies.read. Every order placed for the company, newest first, on account or not. `placed_by` is masked on a demo store.
Requires companies.read. By country, state and prefix.

post.description: Requires companies.write. An area — a country, a state in it, a postcode prefix in that — that sends this dealer the enquiries from it. A territory has one dealer: an area another dealer already has is refused, naming them.

400.description: `country` is not a two-letter code, `state` is too long, or `postal_prefix` is not letters and digits or is longer than 16.

409.description: Another dealer already covers exactly that area.

delete.description: Requires companies.write. Leads already routed stay with the dealer.

404.description: The company has no such territory.

get.summary: Every company's orders, for chasing payment
get.description: Requires companies.read. Every company's orders placed on account, newest first — the ledger a store chases payment from; an order paid for at checkout is owed nothing and is not in it. `overdue=true` narrows it to orders past their due date and still unpaid. An order on account is settled with `POST /api/admin/orders/{id}/mark-paid`. `placed_by` is masked on a demo store.

get.summary: One order in a company's ledger
get.description: Requires companies.read. Which company an order was placed for, its PO number, whether it is on account, when it is due and whether it is overdue, and the approval or quote it came from. `placed_by` is masked on a demo store.

400.description: The order id is not a positive integer.

404.description: The order was not placed for a company, or does not exist.

get.description: Requires companies.read. Newest first. Read-only: approving is the company's decision, made by its own approvers, not the store's. `requested_by_email` is masked on a demo store.
Requires quotes.read. Newest first; `status=requested` is the queue waiting for a price. `requested_by_email` is masked on a demo store.
Requires quotes.read.

put.description:
Requires quotes.write, which by default only a manager holds: a quote is a price. `lines`, when given, replace the quote's lines — the store may change a quantity or add what the buyer forgot — each with its `unit_price_minor`; `reply` is the store's note to the buyer; `expires_at` is when the offer lapses. A field left out is left alone. Lines may stay unpriced while the work is in progress; sending needs every one priced.

Afterwards the quote is `requested`, whatever it was: changing a sent quote takes it back, so the buyer cannot accept a price being rewritten under them, and it has to be sent again. An expired quote re-priced this way needs a new `expires_at`, or sending it is refused.

400.description: `lines` is an empty array; a line has no positive quantity or a negative price; or a variant is listed twice or does not exist.

403.description: Requires quotes.write; or a line is outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`, with each such line in `details` as `{variant_id, sku, reason}`): the buyer could not accept a quote holding one, so it cannot be written.

409.description: The quote is accepted, declined or cancelled, and can no longer be changed.

post.summary: Send a priced quote to the buyer
post.description: Requires quotes.write. Only a `requested` quote with every line priced can be sent. It is on offer until its `expires_at`, or for thirty days when it has none unless the store configured otherwise, and the buyer who asked is emailed (`b2b.quote_ready`). From then it is `quoted` and can be accepted, until it reads `expired`.

400.description: A line has no price, or `expires_at` is in the past.

403.description: Requires quotes.write; or a line is outside the company's catalogue (`not_in_catalogue`, with each such line in `details` as `{variant_id, sku, reason}`), the catalogue having narrowed since the quote was priced.

409.description: The quote is not `requested`: it has been sent already, or is accepted, declined or cancelled.

post.description: Requires quotes.write. Closes the quote without an order, whether it was waiting for a price or already sent; `declined_by` is `store`. Nobody is emailed.

409.description: The quote is already accepted, declined or cancelled.

get.description: Requires companies.read. The whole network, by country, state and prefix: for a map, or to see who covers where.

Requires companies.read. Every catalogue by name, with how many categories, products and companies each has. `q` matches part of the name. A catalogue is what a company held to it may buy: every product filed under one of its categories or anything beneath them — read from core's category tree as it stands at the moment of the check — and its products one by one. A company with no catalogue buys everything. The checkout guard, quick order, a file, a repeat order and a quote all hold to it; the public storefront still lists every product to a signed-in company buyer, and the guard is what holds the line.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the name, in any case.

post.description: Requires companies.write. A name, unique, and the categories and products it allows. Every id must exist; repeats are dropped. At most 1000 categories and 5000 products.

400.description: No name; an id that is not a positive integer or names nothing; or more than the limit.

409.description: A catalogue with that name already exists.

get.description: Requires companies.read. The catalogue with its ids, each named as core reads it now — a category by its full path — and `missing` on one deleted since, which allows nothing.

patch.description: Requires companies.write. Every field is optional; `category_ids` and `product_ids`, when given, replace the lists. A company held to it is held to the new lists from its next basket and its next checkout, and an approval or a quote placed afterwards is checked against them.

400.description: An empty name; an id that is not a positive integer or names nothing; or more than the limit.

409.description: Another catalogue has that name.

delete.description: Requires companies.write. A catalogue a company is held to is refused, naming the companies: dropping it from under them would let them buy everything.

409.description: A company is held to it.

get.description: Requires leads.read. Newest first. `unrouted=true` is the store's own — the enquiries nobody's territory covers. `email` and `phone` are masked on a demo store.

parameters.name: routed_by
parameters.description: Keeps the leads that reached their holder one way. `unrouted` cannot be combined with `company_id`, nor `territory` or `store` with `unrouted=true`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches part of the name, message or postcode, in any case — and of the email or phone, except on a demo store, where those are masked and are not searched.

400.description: An unknown `status` or `routed_by`, a `company_id` that is not a positive integer, or two filters that ask for different leads: `unrouted` or `routed_by=unrouted` with `company_id`, or `unrouted` with `routed_by=territory` or `store`.

get.description: Requires leads.read. `email` and `phone` are masked on a demo store.

400.description: The id is not a positive integer.

patch.summary: Hand a lead to a dealer, take it back, or say how it stands
patch.description: Requires leads.write. Handing a lead to a dealer emails its admins and approvers (`b2b.lead_routed`) and starts it again at `new`, unless `status` is sent too: how far the last dealer got is not how far this one has. `email` and `phone` in the answer are masked on a demo store.

400.description: Neither field was sent, `status` is unknown, or the company does not exist.

409.description: The dealer is closed and takes no leads.

B2bCustomerID.name: customer_id
B2bCustomerID.description: The buyer's account id, from ext/identity.

B2bOverdue.name: overdue
B2bOverdue.description: `true` keeps only orders on account past their due date and still unpaid. Any other value is no filter.

B2bApprovalStatus.name: status
B2bApprovalStatus.description: Only requests in this state. Empty is every state.

B2bQuoteStatus.name: status
B2bQuoteStatus.description: Only quotes in this state. `expired` finds quotes sent and past their expiry; `quoted` only those still on offer. Empty is every state.

B2bCompanyFilter.name: company_id
B2bCompanyFilter.description: Only this company's. Anything but an integer is a 400.

B2bOrderID.name: order_id
B2bOrderID.description: The order's id, as the company's order list gives it.

B2bLeadStatus.name: status
B2bLeadStatus.description: Only leads in this state. Empty is every state; anything else is a 400.

B2bCountry.name: country
B2bCountry.description: Only territories in this country, a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code. Case does not matter.

B2bUnrouted.name: unrouted
B2bUnrouted.description: `true` keeps only the leads no dealer has: the store's own. Cannot be combined with `company_id`.

B2bOrderSearch.name: q
B2bOrderSearch.description: Matches part of the order number or the PO number, in any case — and of the email the order was placed with, except on a demo store's admin routes, where that is masked and is not searched.

B2bStatementFrom.name: from
B2bStatementFrom.description: The first day the statement covers, YYYY-MM-DD in the store's time zone. Defaults to the first of the month the period ends in.

B2bStatementTo.name: to
B2bStatementTo.description: The day after the last one the statement covers — exclusive, as every range in the engine is — YYYY-MM-DD in the store's time zone. Defaults to tomorrow, so the statement runs to the end of today.

B2bStatementFormat.name: format
B2bStatementFormat.description: `csv` answers the statement as a text/csv file. Anything but `json` or `csv` is a 400.

B2bCompany.description: A business that buys from the store.

code.description: Lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens; unique.

status.description: `on_hold` stops new orders on account and nothing else: the company still buys, paying up front, until somebody lifts the hold. `closed` stops it ordering at all.

group_id.description: The customer group whose prices the company's buyers get. A group deleted since leaves the company pricing as everybody does.

credit_limit.description: null: the company has no account and pays up front.

net_days.description: Days after it is placed that an order on account falls due.

approval_threshold.description: An order total above this, placed by a `buyer`, waits for an approver. null: nobody ever waits.

require_po.description: Every order needs a purchase-order number.

catalogue_id.description: The catalogue the company is held to; null lets it buy everything.

catalogue_name.description: The catalogue's name; absent when there is none.

notes.description: The store's own notes on the company.

territory_count.description: How many territories it serves as a dealer. Zero is a company that is not a dealer.

B2bCompanyInput.description: On create, `name` is required and `code` defaults to one made from the name. On patch every field is optional: an omitted field is left alone, and `null` on `group_id`, `credit_limit_minor` or `approval_threshold_minor` clears it. Amounts are minor units of the store's currency. An unknown field is a 400.

code.description: Lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens.

group_id.description: A customer group that exists. null: none.

credit_limit_minor.description: null: no account; the company pays up front.

catalogue_id.description: A catalogue that exists. null: none, the company may buy everything. Recorded in the terms history.

metadata.description: Replaces the whole object when given.

B2bMember.description: One buyer and their role in a company.

customer_id.description: The buyer's account id, from ext/identity.

email.description: The address the company's customer group holds for this buyer. Empty while they have moved to an address they have not yet confirmed: the old one has left the group and the new one joins once identity confirms it. Masked on admin routes of a demo store.

confirmed.description: True when `email` is set — the buyer's current address is confirmed and in the company's customer group. False while it is awaiting confirmation, so a screen can say so rather than show a blank.

role.description: `admin` runs the company's account: buyers, invitations, approvals. `approver` orders without approval and decides other people's requests. `buyer` orders; an order over the approval threshold waits for an approver.

B2bInvitation.description: An open offer to join a company. The token is never in it: it went to the mailbox, and only the mailbox should have it.

email.description: Masked on admin routes of a demo store.

invited_by.description: The address of whoever sent it, or `the store` for a static admin token.

B2bCredit.description: Where a company stands on its account.

limit.description: null: the company has no account.

outstanding.description: Orders on account neither paid nor cancelled.

available.description: The limit less what is outstanding, never below zero. null when there is no limit.

overdue.description: The part of `outstanding` past its due date.

B2bHistoryEntry.description: One of a company's terms changing, or set when the company was created.

field.description: The term, named as the company's input names it.

old_value.description: The value before, as the API takes it; null when it was none, and on a `created` entry.

new_value.description: The value after; null is none — no account, no group.

currency.description: Set on `credit_limit_minor` and `approval_threshold_minor`, whose values are minor units.

actor_email.description: The operator's or buyer's address as it was; empty for a token or the system.

date.description: The civil date in the store's time zone.

credit_minor.description: Zero for a cancellation of an order already paid: that money is a refund, settled on the order.

balance_minor.description: What the company owed once this line was written.

date_source.description: `recorded`: core's own record of the moment. `noticed`: no record survived, and the line is dated when the module first saw it — it happened at or before then.

B2bStatement.description: A company's account over a period. Amounts are minor units of `currency`.

time_zone.description: The store's time zone, in which the dates are civil dates.

to.description: Exclusive: the day after the last one covered.

aging.description: What is owed at the end by whole days past due; the five sum to the closing balance.

B2bCatalogue.description: What a company held to it may buy.

name.description: A category's full path, or a product's title; empty when it is missing.

missing.description: Deleted from the store since: it allows nothing.

name.description: A category's full path, or a product's title; empty when it is missing.

missing.description: Deleted from the store since: it allows nothing.

company_count.description: How many companies are held to it.

category_ids.description: Categories it allows, each with everything under it. Replaces the list.

product_ids.description: Products it allows one by one. Replaces the list.

B2bCatalogueProduct.description: A product the buyer's company may buy.

in_stock.description: Whether one can be ordered now: stock above zero, or a variant that does not count its stock or sells past zero. `available` is 0 for a variant whose stock is not counted, so it cannot say this alone.

price_minor.description: One, in a basket priced as this buyer.

B2bCatalogueCategory.description: A category holding something the buyer's company may buy.

full_name.description: The path from the root, "Apparel / Shirts".

product_count.description: Products the company may buy filed under this category, at any depth.

B2bCompanyOrder.description: An order placed for a company, as its ledger reads it. The order itself is core's, at /api/admin/orders/{id}.

payment_status.description: The order's payment status. An order on account stays `pending` until the store marks it paid.

placed_by.description: The order's email. Masked on admin routes of a demo store.

due_at.description: Present for an order on account only: anything else was paid for at checkout.

overdue.description: On account, past `due_at`, unpaid and not cancelled.

approval_id.description: The approval request the order was placed from, when an approver said yes to it.

quote_id.description: The quote the order was placed from, when it was one.

B2bBuyerOrder.description: An order from the company's list as a buyer reads it: the ledger's fields, and the order itself.

order.description: The order as its shopper is shown it: no access token, no store note, no returns, and only the refunds that moved money.

B2bCheckoutRequest.description: The buyer's own cart, checked out for their company. The email is the account's, so there is no field for it.

cart_id.description: The cart's token, as the public cart routes name it.

payment_method.description: A payment method code. Defaults to `on_account` when the company has an account; required when it has none.

po_number.description: The company's purchase-order number. Required when the company has `require_po`.

payment_data.description: Passed through to the payment provider, as on the public checkout.

return_url.description: Where a redirect-flow gateway sends the buyer back to.

line_ids.description: Check out only these lines of the cart, by the `id` each of its `line_items` carries, and leave the rest in the basket. Empty or absent is the whole cart; every line listed is the whole cart too, and converts it as a whole checkout does.

B2bPlacedOrder.description: An order placed, and what the client must do to pay: the pair `POST /api/checkout/{code}` answers with. On account, `payment.kind` is `none`.

B2bApprovalLine.description: One line of a basket waiting for approval, at the price the approver is asked to approve.

B2bApproval.description: A basket waiting for an approver. Its lines and prices are a snapshot: an approver approves what they were shown, and the order is placed from it, not from a cart the buyer could still be changing.

kind.description: A checked-out cart, or an accepted quote.

status.description: `placing` is an approver's claim while the order is being placed; it ends `approved`, or back at `pending` with `last_error`.

requested_by_email.description: Who asked, as they were when they asked — the request is a record, and a buyer who later changes address or leaves the company still asked for it. Masked on admin routes of a demo store.

total.description: What the order came to when it was submitted, delivery and tax included. Placing it works delivery and tax out again as of the approval.

decided_by.description: The approver's account id. Absent until approved or rejected, and on a request its buyer withdrew.

last_error.description: Why the last attempt to place it failed.

B2bApproved.description: The order an approval placed, in the shape a checkout answers with (`order`, `payment`), and the approval it closed.

B2bQuoteLine.description: One line of a quote. The SKU and title are copied when the line is written, so the quote still says what it was for after a product is renamed.

unit_price.description: null until the store prices the line.

B2bQuote.description: A request for a price and, once sent, the price: agreed for this basket and this company, never a price list a whole customer group would reach.

status.description: `requested` is waiting for the store; `quoted` is sent and on offer. `awaiting_approval` was accepted by a buyer over their approval limit and is held for the approval — it cannot be accepted again, and goes back to `quoted` if the approval is rejected or withdrawn. `expired` is read, not stored: a quoted quote past `expires_at` reads as expired, so nothing has to run at midnight to make it true.

requested_by_email.description: Who asked, as they were when they asked — the request is a record, and a buyer who later changes address or leaves the company still asked for it. Masked on admin routes of a demo store.

declined_by.description: Present once declined: `store`, or the address of the buyer who declined it.

total.description: The lines at their prices. null until every line is priced.

order_id.description: The order it became, once accepted.

unit_price_minor.description: The store's price, in minor units of the store's currency. Ignored on a buyer's request.

B2bQuoteReply.description: The store pricing a quote. Every field is optional; one left out is left alone.

expires_at.description: When the offer lapses. Once set it can be moved but not cleared.

B2bQuoteAcceptance.description: A buyer taking a quote, and where it is going. The email is the account's.

payment_method.description: Defaults to `on_account` when the company has an account; required when it has none.

B2bBulkLine.description: One line of a pasted order. Give a `sku` or a `variant_id`; when both are given the variant id names the variant and the SKU is only echoed back.

quantity.description: At least 1. A line asking for less is rejected (`invalid`), not refused with the whole request.

cart_id.description: The basket to add to, by its token. Absent opens a new one.

B2bRejectedLine.description: A line that did not go into the basket, and why.

sku.description: As asked for, or the variant's own when the line named only a variant.

variant_id.description: Absent when nothing was found to name.

reason.description: `not_found`: no variant has that SKU or id. `inactive`: it is not for sale. `insufficient_stock`: more than is available. `invalid`: the quantity is under 1, or a file's cell is not a number. `inactive` and `insufficient_stock` are the reasons a refused checkout gives for the same two things. `not_in_catalogue`: the company is held to a catalogue that leaves it out; the checkout would refuse it.

message.description: The reason in words, for a person: "only 3 left in stock".

row.description: From a file: the line's row, counting the header as row 1, as a spreadsheet numbers it. Absent for a JSON line.

B2bCartFill.description: A basket after lines were put into it, priced as the buyer, and the lines that would not go.

rejected.description: Empty when every line went in.

B2bTerritory.description: An area one dealer covers. An empty `state` or `postal_prefix` covers all of it: `{US, CA, ""}` is the whole of California.

state.description: Upper case, spaces closed up; the code, for a state given by a name this module knows.

postal_prefix.description: Letters and digits, upper case; spaces and hyphens removed.

country.description: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 code. Case does not matter.

state.description: Empty is the whole country. Matched without regard to case or repeated spaces, and stored as its code when it is a name this module knows. A state is read by its code or, in the United States, Canada, Australia and India, by its name: "California", "ca" and "US-CA" are all `CA`.

postal_prefix.description: Empty is the whole state, or country. Letters and digits, at most 16; spaces and hyphens are ignored, so `SW1A 1` and `sw1a1` are one prefix.

B2bLead.description: A consumer's enquiry from the storefront's dealer form, and who has it. On admin routes of a demo store `email` and `phone` are masked; a dealer's own routes show them, since those are the dealer's customers to call.

product_id.description: Read off the variant when the enquiry named one.

product_title.description: The product's title as it is now. Absent once the product has been deleted.

variant_sku.description: The variant's SKU as it is now, when the enquiry named a variant. Absent once it has been deleted.

company_id.description: The dealer who has it. Absent: the store's own.

routed_by.description: `territory`: matched to a dealer's territory when it arrived. `store`: an operator handed it over. `unrouted`: nobody covers the address, or the store took it back.

B2bLeadInput.description: What the dealer form sends. Every field is bounded, and an `email` or a `phone` is required so the dealer can answer. Single-line fields refuse control characters. Unknown fields are a 400.

phone.description: Digits, spaces and `+ - ( ) .`, with at least five digits.

country.description: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 code. Without one the enquiry stays with the store.

state.description: Reaches a dealer whose territory names this state; without it, only territories that name none. A state is read by its code or, in the United States, Canada, Australia and India, by its name: "California", "ca" and "US-CA" are all `CA`.

variant_id.description: What the enquiry is about, if the form was on a product. Must exist.

product_id.description: Must exist, and be the variant's product when both are given.

source.description: Where on the storefront it was sent from, in the storefront's own words.

B2bLeadUpdate.description: At least one of the two.

company_id.description: Hand the lead to this dealer: it is marked `routed_by: store`, goes back to `new` unless `status` says otherwise, and the dealer's admins and approvers are emailed (`b2b.lead_routed`). `null` takes it back for the store. A closed dealer takes no leads.

B2bUnauthorized.description: No shopper session, or an expired one.

B2bNotABuyer.description: The account buys for no company (`forbidden`).

B2bMemberList.description: Every buyer of the company. Not paginated: there is no `meta`.

B2bInvitationList.description: Every open invitation. Not paginated: there is no `meta`.

B2bCompanyOrderPage.description: A page of the company ledger.

B2bHistoryPage.description: A page of a company's terms history, newest first.

B2bApprovalPage.description: A page of requests for approval.

B2bQuotePage.description: A page of quotes, each with its lines.

B2bOrderPlaced.description: The order is placed: `order` and `payment`, as a checkout answers. `approval` is absent.

B2bApprovalFiled.description: Accepted for a decision, not yet an order: the order is over the company's approval threshold and is waiting for an approver. Only `approval` is set; there is no `order` or `payment`.

B2bCartFilled.description: The basket, priced as the buyer, and the lines that would not go into it.

B2bTerritoryPage.description: A page of territories, by country, state and prefix.

B2bLeadPage.description: A page of leads, newest first.

B2bCompanyOrderResponse.description: One order as its company's ledger reads it.

B2bBuyerOrderResponse.description: One of the company's orders, with its lines.
